title: Giovanni Ribisi's transition into cinematography will be interesting to watch 🤔

commenti.body: Well, the paycheque isn't nearly as good. That's the reason we never saw Jan Debont or Ernest Dickerson or Barry Sonnenfeld return to cinematography - that's not where the money is.

Jan de Bont hasn't directed anything for 20 years.

Money has nothing to do with it.

It's about ego.

It's interesting working in film how much power a DOP has. They decide when to move on to a new set up or scene and can over power everyone to request another take. While they don't talk to actors about motivation or character, they will direct actors to move faster/slower talk at a certain pace, look in certain directions etc. On a TV show, they have more power than a director does in determining a look. That said I don't have enough experience on movies (that aren't crappy Hallmark ones) to speak to the difference between DOPs and directors on those sets.

I am an NZ based Actor who trained as an actor but also work as a DP (gearing up for a feature at start of next year, with a few films currently doing festival circuits)

I get asked all the time if I would Direct but I don’t have the pull to it. It is usually DP or Acting. Depends on the project.

I find that there is a decent overlap between capturing performance and delivering performance… just come at it from 2 pretty different ways.

Will flick my IMDB here… just so you can see I have some legit stuff to my name.

[IMDB](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm6517268/)

Hey there! It's awesome to see someone with both acting and DP skills. If you're ever curious about exploring more casting opportunities or connecting with other industry pros, check out Project Casting. Might be a great way to expand those creative horizons. Cheers!
